scenes.headline: How an 8B model fine-tunes in 4 GB of VRAM
scenes.sub: Soup's layer streaming: 32 layers in host RAM, two on the GPU.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Violet! Soup is a fine-tuning tool that trains an eight-billion-parameter model on a four-gigabyte laptop GPU. Here's how the layers take turns.

scenes.text: Keep the frozen base in pinned host RAM as NF4, and stream it through just two GPU buffers, one layer at a time.
scenes.say: The idea: keep the frozen base in host memory, four-bit quantized, and stream it through just two GPU buffers, one layer at a time.

scenes.title: Why the base is 3.60 GB
scenes.say: First, the size of the frozen base.

parts.note: the packed 4-bit weight: half a byte
parts.say: Half a byte for each packed four-bit weight,
a one-byte scale for every sixty-four values,

parts.note: a nested scale; 112.51 MB a layer, x 32 = 3.600 GB
parts.say: and a tiny nested scale. Across thirty-two layers, that lands on exactly three point six gigabytes.

steps.say: All thirty-two NF4 layers sit in pinned host RAM. The GPU holds just two buffers of a hundred and thirteen megabytes.
While the GPU computes one layer, a prefetch stream loads the next into the other buffer.
Activations are checkpointed. Backward reloads each layer in reverse and recomputes, so every layer is read twice.

steps.note: one buffer is a scheduler bug, not a config
steps.say: Each wait checks which layer a buffer holds, because a buffer recycled too early means silently wrong gradients, not a crash.

scenes.label: faster with every host-to-device byte deleted: compute-bound, not bus-bound
scenes.note: the real cost is dequantizing NF4 on the fly
scenes.say: Is the bus the bottleneck? The project measured it. Deleting every transferred byte makes a step only one point four percent faster.

scenes.text: The whole base never has to fit. Two buffers take turns, and the arithmetic lands exactly on 3.60 GB.
scenes.say: So the model never has to fit at once. Two buffers take turns, and the arithmetic lands exactly where the architecture says.

recap: NF4 base in host RAM: exactly 3.60 GB
Two VRAM buffers, prefetching the next layer
scenes.say: To recap: a quantized base in host memory, two buffers taking turns, and a step bound by compute, not the bus.
